target_customer: Vascular surgeons and dialysis centers (hospitals) performing AV fistula and graft access surgery
problem: Roughly half of dialysis access and bypass surgeries fail, partly because the vein reacts badly after surgery. VenoStent's absorbable wrap goes around the vessel during surgery to keep it open.
business_model: Regulated implantable device sold to hospitals after FDA approval; currently investigational

founders.name: Tim Boire
education: BS Chemical and Biological Engineering and Biotechnology, Tufts University (2008)
founders.background_notes: Developed the polymer biomaterials during his PhD; focus moved to hemodialysis access after the 2014 NSF I-Corps program (YC page).

founders.name: Geoffrey Lucks
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder on the YC page and in InnovationMap coverage.

technical_complexity.rationale: A thermo-responsive shape-memory polymer that is moldable at body temperature with tunable degradation, requiring first-in-human data, FDA Breakthrough designation and a pivotal trial. Biomaterials plus regulatory work is research-grade for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Polymer know-how from a university lab plus a long FDA path (Breakthrough Device 2022, IDE 2023, 200-subject pivotal trial) make fast copying hard.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copying found through the 2024 and 2026 sources reviewed.

market_need_then: VenoStent's seed release states a 55 to 65 percent failure rate for vascular access surgery, over $2B per year in extra CMS cost, and that about 70 percent of ESRD patients rely on dialysis. These are company claims, not independently verified.

branding.domain_note: Uses venostent.com (exact name .com); no purchase history found.

brand_strength.rationale: Press covers funding and FDA milestones, not the brand. Name is a coined stent-like term that fits the vascular focus, but the wrap is not a stent, which may mildly confuse. Brand matters little for a regulated device.

outcome_analysis: VenoStent has progressed steadily through regulatory steps: first-in-human data, FDA Breakthrough Device designation in May 2022, IDE approval in 2023 and first enrollment in a 200-subject pivotal trial in January 2024. It funded this with a 2021 seed, a $16M Series A in 2023 extended to $20M in 2024 and NIH grants. Success now rests on pivotal trial results, which were not found.
notes: Seed release says total funding exceeded $6M including grants and names earlier investors (Texas Halo Fund, Activated Capital, Health Wildcatters, Cougar Ventures, Cowtown Angels) and grants from NIH, NSF and the 2020 KidneyX Redesign Dialysis Phase II prize, with no amounts, so earlier funding is not recorded as rounds. Caplight and PremierAlts list a $10M round in April or May 2026 with conflicting labels; unverified and not recorded. The 2024 NIH grant date is year only. Competitors: the seed release names no rivals and no dated pre-batch competitor for a perivascular wrap was found (Humacyte results address engineered vessels and are dated well after the batch; the Vascular Therapies financing found is from 2022), so the list is empty.
